chunks: Humayd ibn Ziyad from al-Hasan ibn Muhammad ibn Sama'ah from Ja'far ibn Sama'ah that Jamil witnessed one of our companions, and he intended to detach (Khul'a) his daughter from one of our companions.

So Jamil said to the man, 'What are you saying? Have you accepted this which you have taken and left her?' He said, 'Yes.' So Jamil said to them, 'Arise!' They said, 'O Abu Ali! Do you not want the divorce to follow it?' He said, 'No.' And Ja'far ibn Sama'ah used to say, 'The divorce follows it during the waiting period,' and he argued by the narration of Musa ibn Bakr from al-Abd al-Salih (peace be upon him) who said: 'Ali (peace be upon him) said: 'For the woman who is divorced by Khul'a, the divorce follows her as long as she is in the waiting period.'
ai.seo_question: Does Khul'a divorce become final immediately or during the waiting period?
ai.summary: This narration from al-Kafi clarifies the legal status of Khul'a by establishing it as a revocable divorce (Tasree'i) rather than an irrevocable one, ensuring the husband retains the right to reconciliation during the Iddah. Ja'far ibn Sama'ah supports this ruling by citing Imam Ali (peace be upon him) and the tradition of Musa ibn Bakr, highlighting the consistency of the Ahl al-Bayt's jurisprudence on marital dissolution. This distinction is crucial in Shia fiqh for determining the woman's entitlement to maintenance and the procedural requirements for finalizing the separation.
